channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Addresses UN General Assembly's 81st Session
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov delivered a speech at the general debates of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. He congratulated the newly elected president and emphasized Kyrgyzstan's commitment to dialogue and peaceful conflict resolution, offering mediation services.

item.title: Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan Begin Joint Military Exercises 'Birlik Kuchi - 2026'
item.description: Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan have launched joint military exercises named 'Birlik Kuchi - 2026' at the 'Qizilgaya' training center in Azerbaijan's Karabakh region. The drills involve military personnel, equipment, naval forces, aviation, and drones from all three nations. The primary goal is to enhance joint operational readiness and interoperability.

item.title: EU Agrees to Lift Sanctions on Russian Billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman
item.description: EU member states' permanent representatives have agreed to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the sanctions list. This decision was part of a three-year extension of the sanctions program. France and Slovakia had reportedly pushed for Usmanov's removal, citing national security and other reasons.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Select Investors for Energy Projects Through Open Competitive Tenders
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its energy investment project system, selecting investors through open competitive tenders. The new model will first define future electricity needs, then required generation capacity and infrastructure. Responsibilities will be divided among ministries for forecasting, strategic planning, and market regulation.

item.title: Tashkent tests dedicated lane for micro-mobility on Lutfiy Street
item.description: Tashkent is piloting a 2.4-kilometer dedicated lane for micro-mobility on Lutfiy Street. This initiative aims to separate bicycles, electric scooters, and similar vehicles from car traffic and pedestrian sidewalks, addressing safety and convenience concerns in the growing urban transport landscape.

item.title: Tashkent plans to convert central green space into parking lot, sparking public concern
item.description: Tashkent's city administration plans to convert a 1.3-hectare green space near the National Library into a paid parking lot. While promising new pedestrian paths and green areas, the decision has raised questions among the public regarding the loss of urban green space.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches initiative to reward best proposals for cutting bureaucracy
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched the "Bureaucracy-Free Uzbekistan" initiative, allowing citizens and entrepreneurs to submit proposals for eliminating excessive bureaucratic processes in state institutions. Participants can receive cash rewards of up to 2 million soms for their suggestions. The program aims to reduce state body functions by 30% and streamline business requirements.

item.title: China tests world's first underwater perovskite solar power station
item.description: Chinese scientists have successfully tested the world's first underwater solar power system using perovskite solar cells at a depth of 10 meters in the open sea. The technology is designed to efficiently utilize the limited spectrum of sunlight penetrating underwater. The system achieved nearly 35% energy conversion efficiency in laboratory conditions.

item.title: Tajikistan launches 250 MW solar power station in Asht district
item.description: Tajikistan has commissioned a 250 MW solar power station in the Asht district of the Sughd region. The station, built on 793 hectares, is expected to cover about 40% of the region's electricity needs. The project aims to reduce energy transmission losses and increase electricity generation capacity in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reviews Mid- and Long-Term Fuel and Energy Sector Development Plans
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans for the fuel and energy sector's development, focusing on electricity generation and project management. Reforms have increased renewable energy capacity to over 6.3 GW, with solar and wind power contributing significantly. By 2030, Uzbekistan aims for a $300 billion economy and over 41 million people, necessitating accelerated energy capacity growth to meet rising demand.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Austria to Expand Cooperation in Medical Technologies
item.description: Uzbekistan and Austria have agreed to expand their cooperation in medical technologies. Both sides will continue communication between relevant organizations and establish direct partnerships. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Uzbek-Iranian Agricultural Business Forum Opens New Chapter in Cooperation
item.description: An Uzbek-Iranian agricultural business forum was held in Tashkent to expand trade, economic, and investment ties. Discussions covered livestock, veterinary medicine, aquaculture, seed production, and agricultural technology, including drones. The event aimed to foster new projects and partnerships.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sees Decline in Students Studying Abroad
item.description: In the first three months of 2026, 5,862 Uzbek citizens went abroad for education, rising to 7,355 in four months. This marks a significant decrease compared to last year, with 2,600 fewer students studying abroad. Russia remains the most popular destination, followed by South Korea. This trend may reflect the growth of foreign university branches within Uzbekistan and increased overseas study costs.

item.title: China Faces Extreme Weather: Floods and Droughts Hit Amidst Climate Change
item.description: China is experiencing extreme weather conditions, with forecasts predicting an intense rainy season. Since May, the country has been hit by successive waves of floods, including monsoon rains, typhoons, and glacial floods. Provinces like Hunan have reported fatalities and missing persons due to severe flooding, while other regions faced record rainfall and reservoir breaches.

item.title: Toktogul HPP Repairs Three Hydrogenerators in Preparation for Winter
item.description: The Ministry of Energy reports that repairs on three hydrogenerators at the Toktogul Hydropower Plant are underway as part of preparations for the upcoming winter period. The focus is on maintaining generating equipment and infrastructure. Current repairs are being conducted on hydrogenerators G-1, G-2, and G-4, with specific work scheduled for unit G-4 from September 21-26.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Efforts Praised at CIS Interstate Council Meeting
item.description: During the 11th CIS Interstate Council on Combating Corruption in Minsk, Uzbekistan's Anti-Corruption Agency director met with counterparts. Discussions focused on bilateral cooperation, experience exchange, and signing a cooperation program with Russia for 2027-2038.

item.title: First Enrollment Begins for Digital Technology School in Bishkek
item.description: Bishkek has launched its first enrollment for the "School 21" digital technology program, offering free education to Kyrgyzstan residents over 18. The selection process includes online testing and a 14-day in-person "pool" stage. Successful candidates can choose from 22 specializations, including software development and cybersecurity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Proposals to Improve Administrative Justice System
item.description: Uzbekistan has presented proposals to further enhance its administrative justice system, established in 2017. Since its inception, administrative courts have reviewed approximately 150,000 cases, overturning over 70,000 illegal state body decisions and issuing 27,000 private rulings on official misconduct.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Electricity Generation Capacity to 46.1 GW by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to reach 46.1 GW of electricity generation capacity by 2030, producing nearly 129 billion kWh annually. By 2035, capacity is projected to hit 57.2 GW, generating 154.7 billion kWh. These plans were presented to President Mirziyoyev, considering economic growth and rising energy consumption.

item.title: Uztelecom Launches Data Centers in Bukhara and Kokand to Boost AI and Cloud Technologies
item.description: Uztelecom has launched two new data centers in Bukhara and Kokand on September 22. These facilities are intended to support the development of artificial intelligence and cloud technologies within Uzbekistan. The initiative aims to enhance the country's technological infrastructure.

item.title: Program for safe and respectful work environment introduced
item.description: A presidential decree introduces a program to ensure a safe and respectful work environment in state organizations and enterprises with state participation. An information portal will launch by December 1 for reporting pressure and violence.

item.title: Tajikistan's Migration Ministry Warns Citizens Against Sending Money to Unknown Individuals
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor and Migration representative office in Russia urged Tajik migrants not to transfer money to unknown accounts or contact suspicious groups. The office warned that malicious groups and fake funds on social media are using AI-generated content to solicit funds. Involvement with such groups can lead to severe penalties in Russia and Tajikistan.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Attends UN General Assembly General Debate Opening
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov participated in the opening of the general debate at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York on September 22nd. The presidential press service reported his attendance at the event.

item.title: Tashkent Ranks 343rd in Global Cities Index 2026, Shows Strong Growth Potential
item.description: Tashkent secured 343rd place among 1000 major global cities in the Global Cities Index 2026 by Oxford Economics, climbing 128 spots in a year. The report highlights Tashkent as a promising economic hub in Central Asia, noting its diversified economy, construction growth, and stable population increase. Challenges include low GDP per capita and water scarcity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans 16 New Substations and 5,000 km of Power Lines by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to construct 16 new substations, including nine 220 kV and seven 500 kV facilities, along with nearly 5,000 kilometers of power transmission lines by 2030. This was announced at a meeting chaired by the President, focusing on the development of the country's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Presidents Discuss Relations and Regional Issues
item.description: The Presidents of Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan held a phone call on September 22. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and regional agenda items. The leaders also exchanged greetings and well wishes.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Era for Entrepreneurship with Focus on Prevention
item.description: Uzbekistan is shifting its approach to entrepreneurship from control to prevention and from barriers to opportunities. A presidential decree introduced a three-year moratorium on inspections for small businesses, aiming to reduce administrative burdens and foster growth.

item.title: Uzbekistan Emphasizes Soil Analysis for Food Security and Soil Fertility
item.description: Uzbekistan's Center for Agrochemistry and Soil Analysis is conducting systematic studies to ensure food security and soil fertility. In 2021-2026, 3.3 million hectares of arable land were analyzed, with electronic agrochemical maps created for 2.8 million hectares. Over 1,800 tons of substandard fertilizers were prevented from reaching fields.

item.title: Hungarian Prime Minister Opposes Oil Storage Facility Construction for Ukraine
item.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has declared his opposition to the construction of an oil storage facility within Hungary intended for Ukraine. Orbán stated that his party, 'Tisza', will not permit such construction while it is in power, emphasizing his firm stance against the project.

item.title: Uzbekistan to launch portal for workplace pressure and discrimination complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan will gradually implement the 'Safe and Respectful Working Environment' program, designed to protect employees from pressure, violence, discrimination, and harassment in the workplace.

item.title: Bishkek auto repair worker detained on suspicion of drug trafficking
item.description: A resident of the Chuy region was detained in Bishkek on suspicion of involvement in the illegal trafficking of narcotic drugs.

item.title: Illegal tobacco sales worth 2.8 billion Uzbek soms seized in Namangan
item.description: Authorities in Namangan have stopped the sale of illegal tobacco products valued at 2.8 billion Uzbek soms.

item.title: Tajikistan and Germany Discuss Expanding Labor Migration Opportunities
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Labor, Migration, and Employment met with a German company representative to discuss expanding cooperation in labor migration. They focused on creating transparent selection mechanisms for the German labor market, including candidate training and language preparation. Both sides expressed readiness to continue dialogue and strengthen ties.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened in Bishkek Over Sale of Free Textbooks Intended for Students
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Bishkek concerning the sale of textbooks meant for free distribution to schoolchildren. The investigation aims to determine the origin and circumstances of the textbooks' production and sale, and whether they were intended for free provision. A parliamentary committee is reviewing the situation.

item.title: China Hosts Meeting on Uzbekistan's Sustainable Aviation Fuel Production Project
item.description: In Ningbo, China, Allied Biofuels held a FEED meeting for its sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and e-SAF production project in Uzbekistan, valued at $6.1 billion. Representatives from Sinopec, Topsoe, Sasol, and Plug Power attended. Sinopec Engineering Group will conduct FEED, with Topsoe and Sasol providing key technologies, and Plug Power supplying electrolyzer systems.

item.title: Warehouse manager at Namangan kindergarten accused of raping a 5-year-old girl
item.description: A warehouse manager at a state kindergarten in Uzbekistan's Namangan region is accused of raping a 5-year-old girl. A criminal case was initiated on September 12 under Article 118, Part 4 of the Criminal Code. The suspect has been detained and a pre-trial detention measure imposed.

item.title: Uzbek team presents atomic city concept at Global HackAtom championship
item.description: A team from Uzbekistan, "Synthesis," presented a concept for an atomic city at the Global HackAtom international student championship in Yekaterinburg. Their model city utilizes a nuclear power plant for electricity, heat, desalination, nuclear medicine, and industrial production, aiming for self-sufficiency.

item.title: Uzbekistan to expand citizens' right to appeal against state bodies in administrative court
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering expanding citizens' ability to appeal against state bodies in administrative courts. Proposals include introducing four types of claims and allowing appeals without time limits in certain cases, according to a meeting chaired by the President.

item.title: Uzbekistan may grant citizens the right to appeal local government regulations in court
item.description: Uzbekistan may grant citizens the right to directly appeal normative legal acts of local authorities in administrative courts. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to enhance administrative justice, which aims to strengthen judicial oversight and protect citizens' rights.

item.title: Lawyers for Tolekan Ismailova to appeal to UN Human Rights Committee
item.description: Lawyers for Tolekan Ismailova, head of Bir Duino-Kyrgyzstan, will file a complaint with the UN Human Rights Committee after exhausting domestic legal options. This follows the Bishkek City Court's September 21 ruling, which upheld a lower court's decision.
